tasks.title: Load and validate relay configuration from environment variables
tasks.dod: Unit tests assert a complete environment produces a Config with bot token, chat id, shared secret, port, and Telegram timeout; a missing or empty shared secret fails config loading closed rather than being treated as a valid (always-fail) match.

tasks.title: Implement the Telegram sendMessage client wrapper with a bounded timeout
tasks.dod: Unit tests against a faked HTTP layer assert: a successful call resolves delivered; a Telegram chat-not-started response resolves as its own distinct outcome; any other Telegram error resolves as a generic delivery failure; a call that does not respond within the configured timeout (5000 ms) resolves as a timeout failure rather than hanging.

tasks.title: Implement summary validation (reject empty, whitespace-only, or non-text input)
tasks.dod: Unit tests assert a non-empty string with visible characters passes; an empty string, a whitespace-only string, and a missing/non-string value are all rejected the same way.

tasks.title: Implement shared-secret authorization check (fail-closed)
tasks.dod: Unit tests assert the correct secret passes; a wrong or missing secret is rejected without evaluating the summary at all; an unset/empty configured secret always rejects, never matches by default.

tasks.title: Implement the relay orchestration service (auth -> validate -> deliver -> shape response)
tasks.dod: Unit tests with a faked Telegram client assert every branch: wrong secret -> { error: unauthorized } regardless of summary; valid secret + empty summary -> { error: summary must not be empty }; valid secret + summary + Telegram success -> { status: sent }; valid secret + summary + Telegram chat-not-started -> its own distinct wording; valid secret + summary + any other Telegram failure or timeout -> the generic failure wording; no call reaches the Telegram client when the secret or summary check fails.

tasks.title: Add the POST /api/v1/send route and wire config -> telegram -> relay -> http
tasks.dod: The route matches contracts/openapi.yaml's sendSummaryToTelegram operation: reads the X-Chat-Brief-Secret header + JSON body, calls the relay service, and always responds HTTP 200 with the SendSuccess/SendError envelope, even when the request body is malformed or an unexpected exception is thrown, without ever including the shared secret or the Telegram bot token in the response.

tasks.title: Add the end-to-end integration test against a faked Telegram API
tasks.dod: One integration test drives a real HTTP request through the full app to a faked Telegram API and back, asserting: the happy-path round trip stays within the spec's p95 budget; a faked hanging Telegram response is treated as a delivery failure at the 5000 ms timeout, not an unbounded wait; a wrong shared secret never results in a call reaching the faked Telegram API.

tasks.title: Document the required environment variables for deployment
tasks.dod: A .env.example (or README section) lists every environment variable src/config/ reads, with placeholder values only, so the owner can configure a real deployment without reading the source.
